gaps: Zen 5 X3D parts believed to exist but OMITTED because existence/spec could not be confirmed offline: Ryzen 5 9600X3D, Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Ryzen 9 9950X3D2. Emitting a wrong X3D record is the worst failure mode for this catalogue, so these are deferred to the harvest pipeline.
Zen 5 F-suffix desktop parts (Ryzen 5 9500F, Ryzen 7 9700F) omitted — recalled but not confidently verified.
Zen 5 desktop APUs on AM5 (a 9000G / Gorgon Point equivalent to the 8000G line) omitted entirely — no confident knowledge that a retail AM5 Zen 5 APU line shipped.
Ryzen 3 8300G (Phoenix 2, OEM) omitted — L3 configuration not confidently known.
Ryzen 3 5100 (Cezanne OEM) omitted — not confident it reached retail or OEM channels.
Bulldozer/Piledriver OEM-only SKUs omitted: FX-8140, FX-6120, FX-4150. Existence uncertain.
Athlon 3000G is included but the Athlon Gold/Silver PRO 3150G/3125GE OEM desktop parts are omitted (OEM-only, low gaming relevance, specs uncertain).
Sempron 2650/3850 (AM1 socket, Kabini) out of scope — AM1 is not in the requested socket set and the parts are not gaming-relevant.
Athlon II / Phenom II (AM3, pre-FX) out of scope per remit (FX onward).
A6-6400K, A4-series and other 2-core FM2/FM2+ APUs below A6-7400K omitted as not gaming-relevant.
pcieLanes null for Threadripper 7000/9000 non-PRO (TRX50) and for all Phoenix 8000G parts — the exact CPU-provided lane budget was not confidently known.
pcieLanes null for all AM3+ FX parts: those CPUs have no on-die PCIe; lanes come from the 990FX/970 northbridge. pcieGen 2 is recorded as a platform-level value.

MISSING iGPU RECORDS the gpu catalogue must add before these igpuId references resolve (12 refs, 38 CPU records affected): amd-radeon-graphics-raphael-2cu (the 2 CU RDNA 2 iGPU on every non-F Raphael and Granite Ridge desktop part — 20 records depend on it); amd-vega-7-renoir and amd-vega-6-renoir (4600G/4650G and 4300G/4350G); amd-radeon-hd-7660d, amd-radeon-hd-7560d, amd-radeon-hd-8670d (Trinity/Richland); amd-radeon-r7-kaveri-512sp, amd-radeon-r7-kaveri-384sp, amd-radeon-r5-kaveri-256sp (Kaveri/Godavari); amd-radeon-r7-bristol-ridge-512sp, amd-radeon-r7-bristol-ridge-384sp, amd-radeon-r5-bristol-ridge-384sp (Bristol Ridge).

The gpu-amd agent emitted only discrete desktop GPUs (0 igpu records); all AMD integrated graphics currently live in gpu-intel.json. Whichever agent owns that namespace needs to fill the 12 gaps above.
uncertainties: FX-4320 and FX-4130 L3 size recorded as 4MB (vs 8MB on FX-4300's siblings FX-4350/FX-4170). Moderate confidence; FX-4300 at 4MB L3 is high confidence.
FX official memory speed recorded as DDR3-1866 across the whole line. Some early Zambezi SKUs may be rated DDR3-1600.

AVX2 set true only for Excavator parts (Athlon X4 845, A12-9800/A10-9700/A8-9600/A6-9500, Athlon X4 950). Bulldozer/Piledriver/Steamroller set false (AVX 1.0 + FMA4/FMA3 only). Moderate confidence on the Excavator AVX2 claim.

Ryzen 5 8500G / 8400F / (omitted) 8300G mix Zen 4 and Zen 4c cores. caps.hybrid is set FALSE deliberately: unlike Intel P/E, Zen 4c is ISA-identical and SMT-2 on every core, so threads == cores*2 and the pCores/eCores decomposition does not apply. The parts do have asymmetric max clocks, which the model may want to treat separately.
Ryzen 7 8700F and Ryzen 5 8400F: igpuId set null. I am not confident whether the F parts fully disable the Radeon 780M/740M or ship a cut-down iGPU. Verify at harvest.

Threadripper 9000 PRO (9995WX..9945WX) base clocks nulled — only the 5.4 GHz boost ceiling is recorded with confidence. Non-PRO 9980X/9970X/9960X base clocks are recorded but mirror the 7000-series values and should be re-checked.
Threadripper 9000 official memory recorded as DDR5-6400; moderate confidence.
Threadripper PRO WX parts use socket sWRX8 (3000WX/5000WX) which was not in the brief's socket list. Recorded factually rather than forced into a listed socket.
officialMemMTs is the 1 DIMM-per-channel single-rank JEDEC rating; AM4 4-DIMM and dual-rank configurations derate substantially and the build model should not read these as achievable speeds.

pcieLanes convention: total CPU-provided lanes including the chipset uplink (24 for Summit/Pinnacle/Matisse/Vermeer/Renoir/Cezanne, 16 for Raven Ridge/Picasso, 28 for Raphael/Granite Ridge). Raven Ridge and Picasso give the GPU only x8; Renoir/Cezanne and all 5000G give x16 but at PCIe 3.0. That x8/gen3 detail is not representable in the current schema.
A8-5600K / A8-6600K-class iGPU slugs and A6-9500 iGPU shader counts not verified; only the id string is emitted here, the GPU agent owns the specs.

igpuId references were reconciled against the iGPU records actually emitted by the gpu-intel agent (which owns the integrated-graphics namespace for both vendors). 12 of 24 distinct references now resolve, covering 27 of the 65 APU records. The 12 that do not resolve are listed in gaps as concrete missing iGPU records, NOT nulled: nulling would falsely assert that these APUs have no integrated graphics.

Athlon 3000G points at amd-vega-3-raven although the part is generally Picasso silicon; its Vega 3 is config-identical (3 CU / 192 SP) and no Picasso Vega 3 record exists. Codename mismatch is cosmetic here.

Ryzen 5 8600G points at the generic amd-radeon-760m (a mobile-context record). The gpu-intel agent made a desktop-specific amd-radeon-780m-8700g for the 8700G but no 8600G equivalent; desktop 760M clocks may differ from the mobile record.
